mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 3.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 20-day returns as investors anticipate sustained low-cost capital.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) within 3 months signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 5-day returns as investors reduce risk exposure to inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 4.0% in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous FEDFUNDS increases (> 0.25pp) and CPIAUCSL declines (> 0.1pp) in 3 months signal contractionary monetary policy amid deflationary demand, producing negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to earnings recession fears.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL falls > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL falls > 0.1pp in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate (UNRATE < 5.0%) during labor market tightening cycles indicates robust job growth, driving positive S&P 500 60-day returns through rising consumer spending and corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: High new housing starts (HOUST > 2200.0) reflect strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, generating positive S&P 500 20-day returns through sustained retail and construction sector growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 2200.0 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) within 3 months signals manufacturing contraction, causing negative S&P 500 5-day returns as recession risks accelerate investor flight.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls > 5.0% in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Joint RSAFS declines (> 0.5%) and FEDFUNDS rises (> 0.25pp) in 3 months signal demand contraction amid monetary tightening, triggering positive S&P 500 20-day returns through anticipatory policy easing.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS falls > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle labor market overheating (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) triggers preemptive monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 5-day returns as inflation concerns override growth optimism.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% monthly (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
